newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's KfW to convert debt to euros in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Germany's KfW to convert debt to euros in 1999.

text.p: German state development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW) said on Wednesday it would convert outstanding mark-denominated debt into euros after the launch of Europe's single currency in 1999.
KfW said in a statement that the move followed the government's decision to do the same.

Although the Bonn government has not officially made a final decision on redenomination, state secretary in the finance ministry Juergen Stark said on Tuesday that Finance Minister Theo Waigel had agreed a proposal that existing debt should be converted into euros from January 1, 1999.
KfW bonds are considered by financial markets as a close substitute for sovereign German debt. Like Germany, KfW has a zero capital risk weighting.
The development agency also said that it expected Germany to adopt the "one cent solution" on debt redenomination, rounding conversions to the nearest cent.

KfW added, however, that bonds currently denominated in other currencies would be converted on a case by case basis according to decisions taken by the relevant European Union countries on conversion of their sovereign debt.
